beats: Eighty thousand dollars of income. Federal tax: zero. Legally. Here's how it works.
Dana has no salary. Her only income in twenty twenty-six is eighty thousand dollars of eligible dividends from Canadian companies.
First, the dividend is grossed up by thirty-eight percent. On paper, her income becomes a hundred and ten thousand, four hundred.
Federal tax on that, after her basic personal amount: about sixteen thousand, five hundred.
Then the dividend tax credit: fifteen percent of the grossed-up amount. About sixteen thousand, six hundred. It wipes out the whole bill. Zero.

The twist: the same eighty thousand as a salary costs about nine thousand, two hundred in federal tax. The credit exists because the company already paid tax on its profits. And provinces add their own rules.
So check what kind of income you earn. It changes the tax.
